newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market not tested - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market not tested - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade was too light to test the market, feedlot sources said.
About 100 steers that will likely grade select and choice sold at $66.00 per cwt in the Texas Panhandle.

Most of this week's cattle sold at $65.00 on Wednesday in active volume as packers moved quickly to restock live cattle inventories, they said. The demand was so strong that most showlists were sold out for the week, including carryover from last week's slow sales.
Cattle feeders said attention was now focused on this afternoon's USDA Cattle-On-Feed Report.
Analysts expect the report to show an average 115.6 percent of a year ago in on-feed supplis as of Aug 1. July placements were expected at 100.8 percent and July marketings at 105.5 percent.

Barring any surprises, especially in the placements figure, fed cattle prices next week were seen steady-firm amid projections for smaller numbers of market-ready cattle on showlists, feedlot sources said.
Prices also could be underpinned by ideas that beef prices would continue the rebound started on Thursday, they said.
